claim: SiT (Ma, Goldstein, Albergo, Boffi, Vanden-Eijnden, Xie, 2024) is built on the DiT backbone but swaps the diffusion formulation for an interpolant framework that connects two distributions more flexibly than standard diffusion.
quote: a family of generative models built on the backbone of Diffusion Transformers (DiT)... the interpolant framework, which allows for connecting two distributions in a more flexible way than standard diffusion based models

claim: SiT modularly studies four design choices decoupled from architecture: discrete vs continuous time learning, the model prediction target, the interpolant connecting the distributions, and deterministic vs stochastic samplers.
quote: we are able to carefully explore various design choices distinctly from the model architecture: using discrete vs. continuous time learning, deciding the objective for the model to learn, choosing the interpolant connecting the distributions, and deploying a deterministic or stochastic sampler

claim: SiT surpasses DiT uniformly across model sizes on conditional ImageNet 256 using the exact same backbone, parameter count, and GFLOPs, and by tuning the diffusion coefficient separately from learning reaches FID-50K of 2.06 (2.62 at 512).
quote: SiT surpasses DiT uniformly across model sizes... using the exact same model structure, number of parameters, and GFLOPs. By exploring various diffusion coefficients, which can be tuned separately from learning, SiT achieves an FID-50K score of 2.06

claim: The official PyTorch SiT repo (~1.2k stars) ships the model implementation, class-conditional ImageNet-256 pretrained weights, and a DDP training script; the best FID-50K of 2.06 is from the XL/2 model at 256x256.
quote: SiT achieves an FID-50K score of 2.06... Pre-trained class-conditional SiT models trained on ImageNet 256x256... A SiT training script using PyTorch DDP
